definition: Ensembling models by training a meta-learner on their outputs — the combiner learns when each base model is trustworthy.
details: Ensembling models by training a meta-learner on their outputs — the combiner learns when each base model is trustworthy.

explainer.lead: Stacking ensembles models by training a meta-learner on the outputs of several base models. It matters because the combiner can learn when each base model is trustworthy rather than averaging blindly.

tiers.eli5: It's like asking several experts for their opinion and having a manager who knows each expert's strengths decide how much to trust each one.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train diverse base models, collect their predictions, and fit a meta-learner on those predictions as features. A pitfall is leakage if the meta-learner is trained on the same data the base models saw.
tiers.paperLevel: An ensemble method in which a meta-learner is trained on the outputs of base models so the combination adapts to which base model is reliable.

explainer.example: Three classifiers predict whether an email is spam; a meta-learner trained on their outputs learns to weight the most accurate one more heavily.
